items.text: Record a payment whenever one happens, in either direction and for any amount. Choose "I paid" or "they paid me" from Home or from the Add screen's new Payment switch.
Paying more than you owe now works: the balance simply flips, and the payment screen shows where you'll stand before you save.
Balances read as plain sentences, like "Jaya owes you $40.00", instead of plus and minus signs.
Each line on The Tab says what it meant for you: you lent, you borrowed, you paid, or you received.

headline: One Add button on the Recurring page

items.text: Fixed the Recurring page on an open iPhone Duo showing two identical + buttons in the side bar. You now add a recurring expense from the end of the list.

headline: The Tab and You use both halves of iPhone Duo

items.text: On an open iPhone Duo, The Tab shows your expenses on one half of the screen and the group's balance on the other. Tapping an expense opens it for editing in place of the balance.
On an open iPhone Duo, the You tab keeps its menu on one half and opens Members, Categories, Recurring, and Invite codes on the other, instead of in a separate sheet.
Fixed custom categories being grouped into a single Other box in the Insights and Home spending blocks. Each custom category now has its own box.

headline: A matching look for your group settings

items.text: Members, invite codes, categories and recurring expenses now match the rest of Divide's receipt look. Members and Invite Codes also have a Done button.
Fixed a blank screen on iPhone Duo when tapping Add a second time while unfolded.
Fixed a category's name appearing a second time as a large heading at the top of its Insights page, most noticeable on a closed iPhone Duo.

headline: Fuller Home on iPhone Duo and iPad

items.text: On an open iPhone Duo or an iPad, Home now shows this month's spending as category blocks beside your recent activity. Tap a block to open that category in Insights.
Choosing a category, month, group, tab, or expense now gives a light tap of haptic feedback.
Fixed the month picker in Insights on an open iPhone Duo, which opened too small to choose a month.
Fixed Insights sometimes showing the wrong category's details after switching months.

headline: A new Insights, made for iPhone Duo

items.text: Insights shows your spending as blocks sized by category. Tap a block to see that category's total, how it compares to last month, and its expenses, then swipe to the next category.
A spending line compares this month so far with last month, so you can see whether you're ahead or behind. Pick any month or year to look back.
On iPhone Duo, Insights opens as two pages: categories on one side and details on the other. Half-fold it and the chart stands up while the controls stay within reach.
Sign-in, setting up your name, and creating or joining your first group now match the rest of Divide.
The keys on the amount keypad now respond anywhere on the key, not only on the number.
Add an expense, check balances, settle up, or see what your group spent this month by asking Siri, for example "Add an expense in Divide".
Divide actions are available in the Shortcuts app, including finding and deleting expenses, so you can build your own automations.
An expense added with Siri shows a summary card with an Undo button, and appears in the app right away. Settling up and deleting ask you to confirm first.
On an open iPhone Duo, every tab uses the full screen again, with Home and Insights set in two columns either side of the fold.
On an open iPhone Duo, tapping Add or an expense slides the register in beside the tab. Hide puts it away and keeps what you've typed for next time.
Fixed the amount keypad sitting small in the corner of the register on an open iPhone Duo.
Fixed the category list when adding an expense showing old names after a category was renamed or added.

headline: A better layout for iPhone Duo

items.text: When iPhone Duo is open, every tab has an add-expense panel beside it, so you can enter an expense while you look over your balances or the tab.
On open iPhone Duo, tapping an expense in The Tab or Lately opens it for editing in that panel. Anything you were halfway through adding is kept until you finish the edit.
When iPhone Duo is closed, the Add button sits with the tab buttons along the side of the screen.
On iPhone Duo, Home and Insights split their two columns along the fold, and the Add button sits in the side bar above the tabs.
When the screen is wider than tall, The Tab shows an expense's details beside the list, and the Add screen puts the amount entry next to the register.
Unfolding or rotating while adding an expense keeps the amount and your place.

headline: Groups carry on when someone deletes their account

items.text: If someone deletes their account, any balance left with them shows as Former member, and you can settle it as usual.
When a group's only owner deletes their account, the member who has been in the group longest becomes the owner.
Fixed the member count on Home including people who had already left the group.

headline: Your name from Apple, and account settings

items.text: Divide uses the name you share when you sign in with Apple, so there's no display name to set up. Change it anytime under You → Display name.
The privacy policy and support pages are linked from the You tab and the sign-in screen.
Deleting your account now asks you to confirm with your Apple ID, and disconnects Divide from it.
Fixed account settings, including Delete account, being out of reach before you joined a group. They're now under Account on the start screen.
Recurring expenses return: set up rent, bills, and subscriptions once, and Divide adds each expense when it comes due.
Recurring expenses can use your group's own categories, and keep working if a category is later archived.
On a full-screen iPad, text is larger so the receipt layout is comfortable to read.
Insights stays on screen while a new month or range loads, instead of flashing a loading page.

headline: Divide on iPad, and any past month in Insights

items.text: Divide now runs on iPad, in any orientation and in Split View, with keyboard shortcuts like ⌘N to add an expense.
Browse any past month in Insights, back to your group's first expense.
Sort a category's expenses by date or by amount.
Insights names the month you're looking at, like "Biggest in June", and months you've just viewed open instantly.

headline: Faster entry and a deeper Insights

items.text: Add several expenses in a row: the Add sheet stays open after you save, keeps a running list of what you added, and lets you undo the last one.
Insights now covers the past 3, 6, or 12 months or all time, compares spending with earlier periods, and lets you tap a category to see its expenses.
The Tab points out expenses filed under Other, so you can move them to a better category.
Every expense shows its category icon, and the tab bar and add button have a cleaner look.
Rename the built-in categories, or add your own, from the You tab. Each group keeps its own list.
Adding or editing an expense offers your group's categories, including the ones you've made.
Change an expense's date when you add it, for something you paid for earlier.
Fixed the date picker choosing a date while you were still scrolling through months.
Balances show a plus or minus sign as well as colour, and every expense shows what it means for you.
Expenses show who paid, and who added them when that's someone else.
Split an expense in one tap: 50/50, or one person owes all of it.
Home shows the last eight expenses, and you can pull down to refresh.
Adding an expense explains what's missing instead of quietly not saving, and the keypad steps aside while you type a note.
Set up rent, subscriptions, and other repeating costs once, weekly, every two weeks, monthly, or yearly, and Divide adds each expense when it comes due.
When a recurring expense starts in the past, Divide shows how many expenses it will add and their total before adding them.
Delete your account from the You tab. Expenses you shared stay in your groups' records without your name.
If your session ends, Divide takes you back to sign-in and tells you why, instead of showing connection errors.
Divide stays in portrait on iPhone, where its layout is designed to be read.
Fixed editing an expense in some languages and regions changing its amount, such as $12.34 becoming $1,234.00.

headline: Add Expense from your Home Screen

items.text: Press and hold the Divide icon on your Home Screen and choose Add Expense to jump straight to a new expense.

headline: A new look: the receipt tab

items.text: Divide has a new design that reads like a shared receipt, with Home, The Tab, Insights, and You tabs and a button in the middle for adding an expense.
Home opens on your main group and shows where you stand, this month's spending by category, and the latest expenses.
The Tab lists every expense by month, with the running balance at the bottom.
Insights shows the month's total, a breakdown by category, and how spending has changed over recent months.
Settle up records a payment between you in one step, and you can switch groups from a sheet on Home.
Better VoiceOver labels throughout the app.
Add an expense straight from your group list. Divide picks the group you last added to, and you can switch groups in the form.
Each group in your list now shows your balance with that group, so you can see where you stand without opening it.
Activity is grouped by day, and each expense shows an icon for its category.
On a group's balances, your own row comes first and stands out from everyone else's.
Quick Add puts the cursor in the amount right away, shows the currency, and has a key to move on to the description.
Fixed group balances going blank when you opened a group while the list was still refreshing.
